title: A Tiny meme that aims for something bigger: AGI
author: Few_Possible_4547
selftext:
Open-source AGI is moving faster than anyone is talking about it.

There is an actual ecosystem being built around $tiny and the end goal isn't just another meme narrative.

**It's AGI.**

$TINY is a community-run coin built around Tiny, the mascot connected to the OpenHuman/TinyHumans ecosystem. The community is building around open-source AI, tools, content, bots, community infrastructure and eventually a much bigger vision around open-source AGI.

And this is where I think the potential gets interesting.

**The AGI angle**

The thesis is pretty simple:

AI is probably going to be one of the biggest technological shifts of our lifetime.

AGI could be even bigger.

Instead of simply making another meme token around "AI", $TINY is trying to connect the meme/community layer with an actual open-source AGI ecosystem.

Tiny already lives inside OpenHuman and is part of the wider TinyHumans ecosystem. There are also projects such as tiny.place and prmpt.cash being developed around the broader ecosystem.

So the meme isn't completely detached from the technology.

**The meme is the front door. The ecosystem is what's behind it.**

And that's a pretty powerful combination if the AI/AGI narrative continues accelerating.

**The burns are actually part of the system**

Another thing I find interesting is the deflationary model.

The website currently shows **34M+ $TINY burned**, with burns coming from both community activity and the permanent buyback-and-burn mechanism.

10% of fees and revenue is allocated to buying $TINY from the open market and burning it.

That means the supply is designed to move in only one direction.

And the community can participate directly in burns as well, with burns being tracked publicly on the Burn Dashboard and leaderboard.

It's not just:

*"number go down because tokenomics spreadsheet says so."*

People are actually participating in the process.

  
FEE distribution:

\- 10% for buybacks and burns

\- 10% community rewards

\- 30% charity vault

\- 50% community vault

**And now there's a reward system for actually DOING something**

This might be one of the most underrated parts of $TINY.

The community recently launched the **Tiny Track & Rewards Board**.

Verified members can earn points for actual contributions — creating content, making videos, Reddit posts, X content, Telegram work, moderation, translations, community calls, contests, tools, bots and much more.

There are already **100+ different tasks** in the catalogue.

Your contributions get reviewed, tracked and displayed publicly, while rewards are distributed through Activity, Burn and eventually Staking pools.

The system also has different activity levels — Tiny Helper, Tiny Contributor and Tiny Core — meaning that simply being active in the community can unlock access to more substantial tasks and rewards.

**That's a very different approach from "buy the coin and pray."**

It gives people a reason to participate.

Create something.

Help the community.

Make memes.

Build tools.

Burn tokens.

Contribute.

Get recognized.

Get rewarded.

And do it again.

**The community is growing globally**

Another thing worth watching is how international the community is becoming.

Tiny has active communities across places like Japan, China, Europe and the US, while the ecosystem is expanding across Telegram, X, Discord, Reddit, Instagram and other platforms.

That's important for a meme.

Because the strongest memecoins aren't just tokens.

They're **identities**.

And Tiny is starting to develop one.

The yellow little guy in pixel sunglasses is becoming the recognizable face of a much bigger story.

That's exactly why the current stage is interesting to me.

You're looking at a community-run token with:

• A fixed supply  
• No tax  
• Burned liquidity  
• Renounced contract  
• 34M+ tokens already burned  
• Permanent buyback & burn mechanics  
• A growing global community  
• A public contribution/reward system  
• An expanding ecosystem of AI-related projects  
• Open-source development  
• And arguably one of the biggest narratives imaginable sitting at the end of the roadmap:

  
**Tiny is tiny right now.**

The idea behind it isn't.
